_comment: Copy this over %ProgramData%\PPPoEAutoDial\settings.json to override the built-in defaults. Every key is optional; anything omitted keeps the built-in value. Changes take effect on the next run - no reinstall needed.
_timing: wait this long after being woken up before the first dial attempt
_per_run_bounds: how long one process may live, and how long it may keep trying
_pacing: never dial faster than Min, never wait longer than Max between attempts
_first_failure_pause: attempt 1 still fires after FirstAttemptDelaySeconds; this is the gap AFTER that first failure. Cadence becomes 20s -> 180s -> 40s -> 60s -> 60s. Raise it if your provider needs longer to release the old session (RAS 628 on every early attempt).
_success: session continuously up for this long counts as healthy, run ends
_lock: time-based self-lock, plus immediate lock on these RAS error codes (651 = port wedged, 756 = dial already in progress)
_policy: 1 = if the machine already reaches the internet by another path (USB tethering, wifi), do not dial
_account: broadband account name for the 'rasdial <entry> <account>' form. Empty = detect it from the RasMan 20267 event log. Only the account name is read here - the password is never touched.
_probes: any single successful TCP connect counts as reachable
_dial: rasdial is killed after this long. The rasphone dialog gets a much shorter 12 s leash, because it only ever finishes quickly when the port is actually ready - otherwise it just parks a dialog that can never succeed.
